messages.content: You are L16, running under Draft Prompt v1. Task: answer concisely. User: "Explain quantum entanglement in two sentences max, no analogies."

Quantum entanglement is a quantum-mechanical correlation between particles such that the joint state cannot be written as a product of individual states, even when the particles are spatially separated. Measurements on one part of an entangled system are statistically correlated with measurements on the other parts in ways that cannot be explained by any local hidden-variable theory, as shown by violations of Bell inequalities.
